'''Don Bernard Zagier''' (born 29 June 1951) is an American-German mathematician whose main area of work is [[number theory]]. He is currently one of the directors of the [[Max-Planck-Institut für Mathematik|Max Planck Institute for Mathematics]] in [[Bonn]], Germany. He was a professor at the ''[[Collège de France]]'' in Paris from 2006 to 2014. Since October 2014, he is also a Distinguished Staff Associate at the International Centre for Theoretical Physics ([[ICTP]]).<ref>[http://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/media-centre/news/2014/10/an-international-mathematician-for-ictp.aspx ICTP News Item]</ref> Among his doctoral students are [[Fields Medal|Fields medalists]] [[Maxim Kontsevich]] and [[Maryna Viazovska]].

== Background ==
Zagier was born in [[Heidelberg]], [[West Germany]]. His mother was a psychiatrist, and his father was the dean of instruction at the [[American College of Switzerland]]. His father held five different citizenships, and he spent his youth living in many different countries. After finishing high school (at age 13) and attending [[Winchester College]] for a year, he studied for three years at [[MIT]], completing his bachelor's and master's degrees and being named a [[Putnam Fellow]] in 1967 at the age of 16.<ref name="MMA">{{cite web|title=Putnam Competition Individual and Team Winners |url=http://www.maa.org/programs/maa-awards/putnam-competition-individual-and-team-winners |publisher=[[Mathematical Association of America]]|access-date=December 13, 2021}}</ref> He then wrote a doctoral dissertation on [[characteristic class]]es under [[Friedrich Hirzebruch]] at [[University of Bonn|Bonn]], receiving his PhD at 20. He received his Habilitation at the age of 23, and was named professor at the age of 24.<ref name="DZRetiree">{{cite web |title=Don Zagier |url=https://www.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/node/97 |website=Max Planck Institute for Mathematics |access-date=19 November 2020}}</ref>

== Work ==
Zagier collaborated with Hirzebruch in work on [[Hilbert modular surface]]s. Hirzebruch and Zagier coauthored ''Intersection numbers of curves on Hilbert modular surfaces and modular forms of Nebentypus,''<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1007/BF01390005 |title=Intersection numbers of curves on Hilbert modular surfaces and modular forms of Nebentypus |first1=Friedrich |last1=Hirzebruch |authorlink1=Friedrich Hirzebruch |first2=Don |last2=Zagier |authorlink2=Don Zagier |journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]] |volume=36 |pages=57–113 |year=1976|bibcode=1976InMat..36...57H |hdl=21.11116/0000-0004-399B-E |s2cid=56568473 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> where they proved that intersection numbers of algebraic cycles on a [[Hilbert modular surface]] occur as Fourier coefficients of a [[modular form]]. [[Stephen Kudla]], John Millson and others generalized this result to intersection numbers of algebraic cycles on arithmetic quotients of symmetric spaces.<ref>{{Cite journal |url=http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS?verb=Display&version=1.0&service=UI&handle=euclid.dmj%2F1077242496&page=record |journal=[[Duke Mathematical Journal]] |volume=86 |number=1 |year=1997 |pages=39–78 |first=Stephen S. |last=Kudla |authorlink=Stephen S. Kudla |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303221306/http://projecteuclid.org/DPubS?verb=Display&version=1.0&service=UI&handle=euclid.dmj%2F1077242496&page=record|url-status=dead|title=Algebraic cycles on Shimura varieties of orthogonal type |doi=10.1215/S0012-7094-97-08602-6 |archivedate=March 3, 2016|via=[[Project Euclid]] and [[Wayback Machine]]|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

One of his results is a joint work with [[Benedict Gross]] (the so-called [[Gross–Zagier formula]]).  This formula relates the first derivative of the [[L-function|complex L-series]] of an [[elliptic curve]] evaluated at 1 to the height of a certain [[Heegner point]].  This theorem has some applications, including implying cases of the [[Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture]], along with being an ingredient to [[Dorian Goldfeld]]'s solution of the [[class number problem]]. As a part of their work, Gross and Zagier found a formula for norms of differences of singular moduli.<ref name="auto">{{Cite journal | url=http://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/zagier/files/doi/10.1007/BF01390325/fulltext.pdf |doi = 10.1007/BF01390325|title = The Euler characteristic of the moduli space of curves|journal = Inventiones Mathematicae|volume = 85|issue = 3|pages = 457–485|year = 1986|last1 = Harer|first1 = J.|last2 = Zagier|first2 = D.|bibcode = 1986InMat..85..457H|s2cid = 17634229}}</ref> Zagier later found a formula for traces of singular moduli as Fourier coefficients of a weight 3/2 [[modular form]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Zagier |first=Don |author-link=Don Zagier |title=International Press Conference on Motives, Polylogarithms and Hodge Theory: Motives and Polylogarithms |publisher=International Press |year=2002 |isbn=978-1-57146-090-5 |editor-last1=Bogomolov |editor-first1=Fedor |editor-last2=Katzarkov |editor-first2=Ludmil |chapter=Traces of Singular Moduli |chapter-url=https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/zagier/files/tex/TracesSingModuli/fulltext.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251130032051/https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/zagier/files/tex/TracesSingModuli/fulltext.pdf |archive-date=30 November 2025 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Zagier collaborated with John Harer to calculate the [[orbifold]] [[Euler characteristic]]s of [[moduli space]]s of [[algebraic curve]]s, relating them to special values of the [[Riemann zeta function]].<ref name="auto"/>

Zagier found a formula for the value of the [[Dedekind zeta function]] of an arbitrary number field at ''s''&nbsp;=&nbsp;2 in terms of the dilogarithm function, by studying [[arithmetic hyperbolic 3-manifold]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |url=http://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/zagier/files/doi/10.1007/BF01388964/fulltext.pdf |doi=10.1007/BF01388964|title=Hyperbolic manifolds and special values of Dedekind zeta-functions |journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]] |volume=83 |issue=2|pages=285–301 |year=1986 |last1=Zagier|first1= Don|bibcode=1986InMat..83..285Z |s2cid=67757648}}</ref> He later formulated a general conjecture giving formulas for special values of Dedekind zeta functions in terms of polylogarithm functions.<ref>{{cite web|title=Polylogarithms, Dedekind zeta functions, and the algebraic K-theory of fields |first=Don |last=Zagier |authorlink=Don Zagier |url=https://people.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/zagier/files/scanned/PolylogsDedekindZetaAndKTheory/fulltext.pdf}}</ref>

He discovered a short and elementary proof of [[Fermat's theorem on sums of two squares]].<ref>{{Cite journal |url=http://portal.acm.org/citation.cfm?id=87107.87119&coll=GUIDE&dl=GUIDE&CFID=15151515&CFTOKEN=6184618 |doi=10.1080/00029890.1990.11995566 |title=Inverse Functions and their Derivatives |journal=The American Mathematical Monthly |volume=97 |issue=2 |pages=144–147 |year=1990 |last1=Snapper |first1=Ernst}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |website=math.unh.edu |url-status=dead  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120205194801/http://www.math.unh.edu/~dvf/532/Zagier |url=http://www.math.unh.edu/~dvf/532/Zagier |archive-date=2012-02-05 |title= One-Sentence Proof That Every Prime p congruent to 1 modulo 4 Is a Sum of Two Squares}}</ref>

Zagier won the [[Cole Prize|Cole Prize in Number Theory]] in 1987,<ref>[https://www.ams.org/prizes/cole-prize-number-theory.html Frank Nelson Cole Prize in Number Theory], [[American Mathematical Society]]. Accessed March 17, 2010</ref> the Chauvenet Prize in 2000,<ref name="NewmanPNT"/> the [[The Karl Georg Christian von Staudt Prize|von Staudt Prize]] in 2001,<ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/200108/people.pdf Zagier Receives Von Staudt Prize.] [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]], vol. 48 (2001), no. 8, pp. 830&ndash;831</ref> the [[Heinz Gumin Prize]] in 2024<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mathematics.uni-bonn.de/en/news/heinz-gumin-prize-for-mathematics-goes-to-don-zagier |title=Heinz Gumin Prize for Mathematics goes to Don Zagier | date = 25 March 2024 |access-date=9 December 2024}}</ref> and the [[Gauss Lectureship]] of the [[German Mathematical Society]] in 2007. He became a foreign member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 1997<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/foreign-members/5046 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160214211132/https://www.knaw.nl/en/members/foreign-members/5046 |title=D.B. Zagier |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |archive-date=14 February 2016 |access-date=14 February 2016}}</ref> and a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] (NAS) of the United States in 2017.
